text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are powerful AI systems that process and generate human-like text. They work by analysing vast amounts of written data, such as books, articles, and websites, to learn patterns in language, grammar, and meaning. When you give an LLM a query, called a prompt, it predicts the most likely next words based on its training. This is known as prompt engineering, where crafting clear questions can improve results. LLMs can write essays, translate languages, and even code. However, they have limits. They can produce incorrect or biased information because they don’t truly understand facts; they only mimic patterns from their training data. So, while impressive, they require careful use.
